# Workspace

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- A **service**: get it with `game:GetService("Workspace")`
- **Not creatable**: it cannot be created with `Instance.new`

The root of the 3D world, available as the global `workspace` and through `game:GetService`. An instance is in the world when it is a descendant of the workspace.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CurrentCamera` | `Camera?` | — | read/write | The camera the world is drawn from. With nil, nothing is drawn. |
| `GlobalWind` | `vector` | `vector.create(0, 0, 0)` | read/write | The direction and speed of the wind, in meters per second. It is visual only: it moves particles that drift with it, foliage, and surface shaders that read it, and it does not push physics bodies. Zero, the default, is no wind. `GetWindAt` returns the wind at a point, including gusts. |
| `Gravity` | `vector` | `vector.create(0, -9.81, 0)` | read/write | The acceleration applied to every unanchored part, in meters per second squared. It is signed: the default is negative and points down. |
| `ScreenSplit` | `Enum.ScreenSplit` | `Enum.ScreenSplit.None` | read/write | How the window is divided between the local players on this machine.<br><br>- `None` draws one picture through `CurrentCamera`. - `Columns`, `Rows` and `Grid` give every local player that has a `Camera` its own view, in the order the players joined: side by side, stacked, or in quarters. - `Dynamic` draws one picture while two players are close together, and splits it along a line when they move apart (see `SplitBlend` and `SplitAngle`).<br><br>Each view is drawn at the resolution of its part of the window, with everything a full picture has. The views share the world, its animation and its reflections, and each has its own culling, shadows, exposure and anti-aliasing.<br><br>While a sequence that takes the camera plays, the window shows one picture; the views return when it ends. The setting is local to this machine and is not replicated. |
| `SplitAngle` | `number` | `0` | read/write | With `ScreenSplit` set to `Dynamic`: the direction on screen from the first player to the second, in degrees. 0 puts the second player to the right of the first, and 90 puts it above. The dividing line runs perpendicular to this direction, and each player's view is on that player's side. |
| `SplitBlend` | `number` | `0` | read/write | With `ScreenSplit` set to `Dynamic`: how far the picture is split, from 0 to 1. At 0 the window shows one picture through `CurrentCamera`. Above 0 the views of the first two local players are joined along a line through the center of the window. The line is `SplitLineThickness` thick at 1 and thinner below it. A game sets this value every frame; `@engine/splitscreen` does it for a top-down game. |
| `SplitLineColor` | `Color3` | `Color3.new(0, 0, 0)` | read/write | The color of the line between two views. |
| `SplitLineThickness` | `number` | `4` | read/write | The thickness of the line between two views, in pixels of a window 1,080 pixels tall. 0 draws no line. |
| `Terrain` | `Terrain?` | — | read-only | The world's terrain, or nil if the world has none. A `Terrain` is an ordinary instance under the workspace, and this property refers to the one the engine uses as the world's ground. |
| `WindGusts` | `number` | `0` | read/write | How much the wind's speed rises and falls in gusts, from 0 (steady) to 1. Gusts travel downwind at the wind's speed, so one can be seen crossing a field. |
| `WindTurbulence` | `number` | `0` | read/write | How much the wind's direction varies from place to place, from 0 (uniform) to 1. |

## Methods

### `GetBodiesInBox(cframe: CFrame, size: vector, params: RaycastParams? = nil): {BasePart}`

Returns every part that overlaps an oriented box, as a new array in a stable order, with one entry per part. `size` is the full extent of the box, as in `BasePart.Size`.

### `GetBodiesInSphere(position: vector, radius: number, params: RaycastParams? = nil): {BasePart}`

Returns every part that overlaps a sphere, as a new array in a stable order, with one entry per part. Use it to find what an explosion reaches or what is within arm's length.

### `GetNearestPlayerDistance(position: vector): number`

Returns the distance in meters from `position` to the nearest player's focus, or `math.huge` when no player has one. A focus is their `ReplicationFocus`, or their character, as the physics step last took them. Use it to decide how much a far thing needs to do; `@engine/npclod` calls an NPC's code by it.

### `GetWindAt(position: vector): vector`

Returns the wind at a point at the current simulation time, in meters per second: `GlobalWind` with its gusts and turbulence. The renderer uses the same function, so a flag, a sail or a sound driven by this value matches what is drawn.

### `Raycast(origin: vector, direction: vector, params: RaycastParams? = nil): RaycastResult?`

Returns the nearest thing that a ray from `origin` hits, or nil. The length of `direction` is the length of the ray, so `direction * 100` casts a ray 100 meters long. When two surfaces are hit at the same distance, the result is the same on every run.

### `Raycast2D(origin: Vector2, direction: Vector2, params: RaycastParams? = nil): RaycastResult2D?`

Returns the nearest `Part2D` or `Tilemap2D` that a ray on the 2D plane hits, or nil. The length of `direction` is the length of the ray. Sensors and parts with `CanCollide` off are ignored. When two hits are at the same distance, the result is the same on every run.

### `RaycastAsSeenBy(player: Player, origin: vector, direction: vector, params: RaycastParams? = nil): RaycastResult?`

Returns what a ray hits in the world as `player`'s machine was drawing it. Every other player's `Character`, and every part with `BasePart.LagCompensated`, is placed where that machine drew it, at the moment it was showing; everything else is as it is now. Check a shot with it on the server, and a player with real latency hits the moving target they aimed at.

The rewind is at most `rewind_cap_ms` under `[network]` in `project.toml`, 200 by default: a slower shooter's shot is checked against the world that long ago, so a target who reached cover more than that long ago is safe. The shooter's own character is where it is now. Only the server calls it; on a client it raises.

### `Spherecast(origin: vector, radius: number, direction: vector, params: RaycastParams? = nil): RaycastResult?`

Returns the nearest thing that a sphere moved along a ray hits, or nil. Use it instead of `Raycast` for a camera boom or a character's ground check, where a thin ray would pass through a gap that the object itself does not fit through.

### `SpherecastAsSeenBy(player: Player, origin: vector, radius: number, direction: vector, params: RaycastParams? = nil): RaycastResult?`

`RaycastAsSeenBy` for a sphere moved along the ray: a thick projectile, or a melee swing, checked against what its player saw.
